rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.9, two-year (2004-2005) field trial in a Cabernet Sauvignon vineyard in Sicily comparing surface drip (DR) with two subsurface drip placements (SDI 0, SDI 120), randomized complete blocks. Q2: Section 3.6 and Table 5, yield per vine was influenced by irrigation system; SDI 120 gave 44% (2004) and 49.7% (2005) higher yield than DR, SDI 0 intermediate; Conclusions state subsurface treatments increased yield with 20% less water. Q4: Section 3.3 and Fig. 1, predawn leaf water potential measured in all treatments (SDI vines reached similar stress with 20% less water); Sections 3.5, Tables 4, 8 and Fig. 3, root contacts, root distribution and root surface per vine measured and related to yield; Table 6 dry-mass partitioning to reproductive organs. Q9: Table 5, yield, cluster and berry weight reported as means <U+00B1> standard errors per treatment and year; Table 7 WUEy with <U+00B1> SE.
rows.notes: Study gives own evidence that SSDI increased yield relative to surface drip, one of the results the review characterises as controversial across studies. Yield measured by a single method (harvest weighing) so no triangulation. Single vineyard, one cultivar, one soil, plot scale. No condition is stated from own findings as a requirement for the yield effect; the Conclusions mention a possible shortcoming of SDI 120 under RDI in sandy soil (reserve storage) and call for further study, but this is not a limitation of the yield result itself (duration, sample, site not discussed as limits), so Q7 and Q8 are no.

notes: Full text appears complete. Treatment effects tested by Tukey HSD with SE reported in tables.
